subject: science
passage: Most animal lineages that give up sexual reproduction seem to die out relatively quickly, a pattern biologists usually explain by noting that sex shuffles genes, helping populations purge harmful mutations and adapt to new threats. Bdelloid rotifers, microscopic animals found in ponds and damp moss, are an apparent exception: no male has ever been observed, and the group appears to have reproduced without sex for tens of millions of years. Genetic studies have offered a partial explanation. Bdelloids can survive being completely dried out, and as their cells repair the DNA damage that drying causes, they seem to take up genes from bacteria, fungi, and plants, acquiring by another route some of the genetic novelty that sex would otherwise supply.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To present a case that seems to defy a general pattern and evidence that may explain it
choices.B: To show that bdelloid rotifers reproduce sexually far more often than biologists had believed
choices.C: To argue that sexual reproduction offers no real advantage to animal populations
choices.D: To explain how bdelloid rotifers are able to survive being completely dried out

explanation.why: The text states a general pattern (asexual lineages die out because they lack the gene shuffling of sex) and then presents bdelloids as "an apparent exception." It closes with a "partial explanation": bdelloids may gain new genes from other organisms, getting "by another route" what sex provides. So the purpose is to present an exception and a possible way to account for it.
explanation.A: Correct. Bdelloids seem to contradict the pattern, and gene uptake during DNA repair is offered as a partial explanation.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says no male has ever been observed; it does not suggest bdelloids reproduce sexually at all.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text accepts that sex supplies useful genetic novelty; its explanation of bdelloids depends on that idea.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Surviving drying is one detail used in the explanation; the text's focus is how bdelloids have lasted without sex.
